title_en: Wheel speed sensor fault (front or rear wheel)
standard_title_en: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The ABS control unit found a fault in a wheel speed sensor circuit, so ABS is probably switched off.
likely_causes_en: Damaged or dirty toothed ring (tone ring)
rider_advice_en: Your normal brakes still work, but ABS is off, so a wheel can lock in hard braking. Ride gently, brake early, avoid wet roads and get it checked soon.
can_ride_reason: brakes work but no ABS; ride gently, brake early, avoid wet roads
technician_hints_en: A bike has front and rear sensors only; check the maker's table for the wheel
Check the sensor gap and the tone ring for dirt and damage
Check the sensor wiring for chafing and the connector for water
held_reason: Chassis wheel-speed entry held until the owner's assistant settles which edition of the chassis code numbering applies: OBDex holds both editions (the same wheel fault sits under two numbers, e.g. C0037 and C0045) and Wal33D reads C0035 as a right front sensor SUPPLY code, not a left front circuit code. Also unresolved: whether 'position-neutral' also rules out front or rear in the text, and the stored standard_title_en still names a wheel. (Review problem 4, sections G, I and J.)

title_en: Gear position sensor A: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the gear position sensor circuit, so it may not know which gear is selected.
rider_advice_en: The gear position signal is unreliable, so the bike may not know which gear is selected. Get it checked soon; if it will not start, do not bypass any safety switch.
can_ride_reason: gear position unreliable; short trip to a workshop
technician_hints_en: Check the gear position sensor connector and wiring
Compare the gear position reading with the real gear
held_reason: P0914 to P0919: the OBDex source is an automatic gearbox selector code (transmission module, harsh shifts, locked in one gear) and the entry maps it onto a bike gear position sensor; the effect on starting was invented. Held until the owner's assistant confirms what these codes mean on a bike. (Review problem 6.)

title_en: Generator (alternator) control: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the circuit that controls the alternator, so the battery may not charge properly.
rider_advice_en: Lights may dim and starting may suffer. A flat battery while riding stops the engine, so avoid night and long rides and get it checked soon.
can_ride_reason: a flat battery stops the engine; go straight to a workshop, no night rides
technician_hints_en: Check the charging voltage at idle and at higher engine speed
Check the alternator control wiring and connector
held_reason: Alternator field or lamp terminal code: an ECU-controlled alternator field or lamp terminal is a car-style feature that small bikes rarely have, and there is no applies_when key to hide it from bikes that cannot raise it. Held until a key such as alternator_ecu_controlled exists. (Review problem 10, section I.)

title_en: Charging lamp circuit: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the circuit of the charging warning lamp (alternator L terminal).
rider_action_basis: charging lamp may not warn you
rider_advice_en: The charging warning lamp may not work correctly, so you may not be warned if charging fails. Get it checked soon.
can_ride_reason: you may miss a charging warning; short trip to a workshop
technician_hints_en: Check the lamp circuit wiring and the alternator connector
Check that the charging lamp lights with the ignition on and goes out when the engine runs
